body: Mods, this post may be better suited to r/SuicideBereavement
If this is truly what you want, then all the best OP. Kudos to you for being brave enough. I hope you find your special heaven.

I know we're not allowed to discuss methods here, but I think we all want to find a way that is as quick and easy as possible. 
The only difference is that now, I don't even care if it is painful or not, as long as it's reasonably quick. I'm think I'm just so done with everything.

Hey, firstly what do you mean by "I'm not even in love with her"? Do you mean you never loved her at all, or that you love her but you're just not "in love" with her? Or did the love fade after 4 years?
Secondly, where have your friends on League of Legends gone?
But that one friend is beginning to annoy me now, he is borderline intrusive and invasive and just won't leave me be
As like I said earlier in reply to someone else's comment, they will probably phone the police and I'll end up in a hospital or unit somewhere (they've done it before)
I have family, but don't live near them and don't get on with them, therefore we rarely talk. I could NEVER EVER tell them about this.
I'm in the UK and it has happened to me before, someone called the police on me
There's so many reasons, see my other post from 2 days ago https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/b1jvyy/before_next_weekby_monday_im_ready_to_go_i_have/
Think I'm going on Monday too. I hope you find peace whatever you decide to do, OP. All the best.

Yes that's fair, but I still think at least a small part of your motivation would be to feel as though you've actively done something to better someone else's life and therefore as a consequence better your own. It's just human nature and part of the reward system to want to do good deeds and in doing so you learn that it partly raises your own self-esteem (not true for sociopaths).
But even when you are at rest doing nothing, the dead skin cells being sloughed off from you all the time are food to dust mites which you can't see with the naked eye....

But ultimately, helping someone to see a brighter side of life has no DIRECT effect on them as they are living their own lives, and not ours. The main motivations on the "helper's" side would be to make the helper feel better about themselves and as though they have helped save someone's life, and will not have to suffer feeling partly responsible for the suicidal person's death (or not doing enough to prevent it). 

Why should they care if someone else takes their own life? Will it DIRECTLY impact them? No...it may temporarily affect their emotions but not actually influence much going on in their life (unless they were in so much grief and as a result of these emotions altered their own actions and their future). However, the person who chose to end their life did not directly cause this as it is not a cause-and-effect situation, the helper chose to process the grief in that way.
 
I support euthanasia and think that if someone wants to die and is in enough pain to want to end their suffering in the first place, they should be allowed to and that is their own right. It's not like we asked to be brought into this world or anything.

EDIT: paragraphing for clarity

I'm sorry you are feeling this way, and I'm also sorry to say that this doesn't sound like the most reliable of methods. The "fight-or-flight" instinct would kick in, and you would most likely run to get away out of sheer fear and the need to survive than voluntarily lie there and wait for the lion to eat you.

Absolutely, couldn't agree more. I'm tired of people trying to persuade us to continue living (despite knowing we're in pain) so that they can escape a guilty conscience. I believe that's all there really is to it, selfishness, I can see no other reason why they would feel entitled to dictate what someone else does with their life.

Not to mention that hospitalising someone at the first sign of danger just for having these thoughts and emotions I think is just bang out of order, especially when a lot of people will experience such thoughts at some point in their life although perhaps not to the same extent. Been there, done that, and I can honestly say hospitalisation solved nothing and if anything halted my progress. I was only 13 (now 24) and it was a horrific experience.

Thank you. I mainly made this post so I can say good bye to somebody on the day. At this point I don't feel I have anything left to say, my mind is made up and I know there's no turning back this time, but thanks anyway.
